### F1 — the pin as restated, and why it cannot go red by the seed

The fixer did not pin the required change's (i) / (ii) literally; it pinned a restated claim and said so (notes row
239, C-0509), which the required change allows ("a sharper true claim may be pinned instead … the bar is a pin that
cannot go red by the seed"). This seat judged the restated pin against that bar by reading the code and by running it.

READ (definition.ts): `judgeCapped(F, chains, X, GRID_CM)` against `judge(F, chains, X)` on the SAME truth —
`gridOfStep(F, GRID_CM)` is `gridOf(F)` (the same loop and float steps); `cappedTruth`'s edge / touching selection is
`spinesOf`'s, and its vertex rule reads the same samples at GRID_CM; `NearBuffer.depth(q, R)` equals `bufferDepth` for
every q whose true depth exceeds −R (the pieces it drops are farther than R = MARGIN_CM + 1 from q, so their depth is
below −R; a sector's negative depth is bounded by its box distance), and returns −R otherwise, which keeps the sign and
the |depth| > MARGIN_CM test; `NearRings.dist` is exact within R. So (a) — the whole verdict on X (X lies in F, its
vertices inside F's box) and the samples' verdict on X + 10 cm — is an identity, not a seed-dependent agreement; the
fixer rightly leaves X + 10 cm's vertices (up to 10 cm outside F's box, beyond the clipped pieces) out of the
comparison with `judge`. (b) — the vertex and simplicity checks of `judgeCapped` read `near` (edge + touching: no
sample) and `fRings`; the step enters only the bucket cell and the samples, so at the capped step they deep-equal those
at GRID_CM: also an identity. (c) — record = arena only where F and every spine's key, route and closedness coincide.
The floors are read from the fixtures and F1's face only (seed-independent): judged 31, same 14, planted 30, by a vertex
or simplicity fault 29, by samples alone 1. Every claim of the fuzz part is asserted per face; nothing counts toward an
assertion on the draws.
